table_title: List the 12 geological periods of the Phanerozoic Eon per the International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS) International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2024/12, as enumerated in Wikipedia's `Geologic time scale` master article. For each, give the era (closed 3-value vocabulary: Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic), start age in millions of years ago (Ma, central value per ICS — ± uncertainty bands stripped per the mirror-precedent asteroids instance), and end age in Ma (per ICS; equals the next-younger period's start age; Quaternary's end age = 0 representing present day). Pre-Phanerozoic eons (Hadean / Archean / Proterozoic) are explicitly out of scope. The deprecated `Tertiary` period name (deprecated by IUGS in 2009) is NOT in scope — replaced by separate Paleogene + Neogene per current ICS framing. `Carboniferous` is one period with Mississippian / Pennsylvanian as subperiods per ICS (US Geological Survey historically used Mississippian + Pennsylvanian as two separate periods, but ICS-standard locked here). Quaternary is a separate period per IUGS 2009 ratification (not a subset of Neogene).
db_analog: SELECT period_name, era, start_age_ma, end_age_ma FROM geological_periods WHERE eon = 'Phanerozoic' ORDER BY start_age_ma DESC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `Geologic time scale` master article, accessed 2026-05-18. Universe is the closed canonical 12-period list of the Phanerozoic Eon per the International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS) International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2024/12. The list has been stable since IUGS ratification of Paleogene/Neogene/Quaternary (2009). source_count = 1 registered (master article supplies universe membership + Era + Start Age + End Age cell values via its consolidated chronostratigraphic table); 12 per-period Wikipedia articles (Cambrian / Ordovician / Silurian / Devonian / Carboniferous / Permian / Triassic / Jurassic / Cretaceous / Paleogene / Neogene / Quaternary) consulted as validation cross-checks during curation but per the artifact contract do NOT count toward source_count and are NOT registered in source_urls — they live in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::validation_cross_checks as provenance prose per the mirror-precedent decade_volcanoes_by_continent (source_count=1 with 16 per-volcano validation cross-checks) + periodic_table_groups_first_three_elements_by_atomic_number (source_count=2 with 18 per-group validation cross-checks). temporal_sensitivity = low because the geological time scale is stable on benchmark timescales — ICS revisions are infrequent and small (last major: 2009 Paleogene/Neogene/Quaternary ratification); v2024/12 boundary values applied per cycle-1 audit's required staging edit. Distribution: Paleozoic 6 periods (Cambrian, Ordovician, Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous, Permian) + Mesozoic 3 periods (Triassic, Jurassic, Cretaceous) + Cenozoic 3 periods (Paleogene, Neogene, Quaternary) = 12 rows. Per-row cells: Period name verbatim from per-period Wikipedia article canonical title; Era per the master article's Era column (closed 3-value: Paleozoic / Mesozoic / Cenozoic); Start Age (Ma) central value per ICS v2024/12 (± uncertainty bands documented in normalization_decisions but stripped from cell value); End Age (Ma) per ICS v2024/12 (equals next-younger period's Start Age in the chained chronostratigraphic order; Quaternary's End Age = 0 representing present day). Boundary value updates per cycle-1 audit-required v2024/12 edit: Ordovician end 486.85 (not 485.4); Silurian end 443.1 (not 443.8); Devonian end 419.62 (not 419.2); Carboniferous end 358.86 (not 358.9); Permian-Triassic boundary 251.902 (not 251.9); Triassic end 201.4 (unchanged); Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary 143.1 (not 145.0); Cretaceous-Paleogene 66.0 (unchanged); Paleogene-Neogene 23.04 (not 23.0).
_extraction_notes: Temporal instance — closed canonical 12-period Phanerozoic universe ordered by geological time (Start Age DESC, oldest first). Single PK Period (period names are unique within the 12-entry universe). Brings `temporal` from gap 3 (2 of 5 staged) to **gap 2 (3 of 5 staged)** — closes the benchmark's LAST remaining gap-3 category. Science family extends from 14 to 15 instances; Science/Geology is a NEW subdomain (no Geology represented in pkdb_bench previously). NEW `time-periods/geological-periods` fine-class extending the MOST-UNDER-REPRESENTED entity bucket `time-periods/*` from 1 to 2 instances (joining `decades` from `programming_languages_by_decade_of_first_appearance`). Source plan: 1 registered source (master Wikipedia `Geologic time scale` article — universe + value role for all 4 cells per ICS v2024/12 conformance) + 12 validation sources (per-period Wikipedia articles) documented in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::validation_cross_checks as provenance prose (not registered URLs per artifact-contract canonical vocab). Mirror precedent for source_count = 1 with validation-prose-only per-entity articles: `decade_volcanoes_by_continent` (source_count = 1 with 16 per-volcano validation cross-checks in prose); `periodic_table_groups_first_three_elements_by_atomic_number` (source_count = 2 with 18 per-group validation cross-checks in prose). claim_type = source_defined — universe is the closed 12-period ICS-canonical list, enumerated in Wikipedia's `Geologic time scale` master article; no curator judgment for universe membership; boundary ages taken verbatim from the master's central values with ± uncertainty stripped per the asteroids precedent. Cycle arc: 1 round of pre-staging design review terminating in 'Approve for Cycle-0 Staging, With 1 Required Staging Edit' (v2024/12 boundary value corrections). Staging edit applied at cycle-0: all boundary values reflect ICS v2024/12 per the audit's specific corrections list (Ordovician 486.85 / Silurian 443.1 / Devonian 419.62 / Carboniferous 358.86 / Permian-Triassic 251.902 / Jurassic-Cretaceous 143.1 / Neogene 23.04 — replacing my preview's older v2012 or earlier values). 4-cell schema (Period composite PK / Era / Start Age (Ma) / End Age (Ma)) at 12 rows = 48 source-grounded cell values. Sort: Start Age (Ma) DESC (oldest first → Cambrian 538.8 first → Quaternary 2.58 last). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include Cambrian (Cambrian explosion / trilobites), Jurassic (dinosaurs / film franchise), Cretaceous (K-Pg extinction / dinosaurs end), Quaternary (humans / ice ages), Era-Period mappings for Paleozoic/Mesozoic/Cenozoic; mid-difficulty cells include Carboniferous (coal-forming forests / coal etymology), Permian (Permian-Triassic Great Dying mass extinction), Devonian (Age of Fishes), Ordovician (jawless fish); harder calibration cells include exact Ma boundaries with v2024/12 central values (e.g., Cambrian start 538.8 vs older 541; Cretaceous-Paleogene 66.0 vs older 65.5; Neogene-Quaternary 2.58), Paleogene vs Tertiary naming controversy (Tertiary deprecated 2009 — should NOT appear in universe), Quaternary status as separate period (ratified 2009, not subset of Neogene). Temporal category-fit: per the temporal category contract, the row universe is ordered along the time axis with Start Age (Ma) as the canonical ranking attribute. The 12-period Phanerozoic chronostratigraphic sequence is the canonical pre-modern temporal-keyed table in geology — direct analog to `summer_olympics_hosts_1960_2020` (year-keyed) and `time_person_of_the_year_2000_2024` (year-keyed), but with a geological-time axis rather than calendar-year. Chips the LAST remaining gap-3 category — closing this single instance gets the benchmark to a uniform-gap-2-or-better state across all 15 categories.
